title: Jesus, While He Dwelt Below
description: Jesus, While He Dwelt Below in Tonic Solfa to RATISBON (WERNER), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Robert Grant wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 452, “The Garden of Gethsemane”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens, six lines (7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to RATISBON (WERNER); any other Sevens, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: Je-sus, while he dwelt be-low, As di-vine his-to-rians say, To a place would of-ten go, Near to Ke-dron's brook that lay: In this place he loved to be, And 'twas named Geth-se-ma-ne.

lines: Jesus, while he dwelt below,
As divine historians say,
To a place would often go,
Near to Kedron's brook that lay:
In this place he loved to be,
And 'twas named Gethsemane.
'Twas a garden, as we read,
At the foot of Olivet,
Low and proper to be made
The Redeemer's lone retreat:
When from noise he would be free,
Then he sought Gethsemane.
Thither, by their Master brought,
His disciples likewise came;
There the heavenly truths he taught
Often set their hearts on flame:
Therefore they, as well as he,
Visited Gethsemane.
Oft conversing here they sat;
Or might join with Christ in prayer;
O, what blest devotion that,
When the Lord himself is there!
All things there did so agree
To endear Gethsemane.
Full of love to man's lost race,
On the conflict much he thought;
This he knew the destined place,
And he loved the sacred spot:
Therefore Jesus chose to be
Often in Gethsemane.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Robert Grant died in 1838.
credits: Words by Robert Grant (1779–1838), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to RATISBON (WERNER) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
